An earlier version flagged single-turn Cowork as substitutable, which inspected well under one percent of one percent of activity and could not support the conclusion. Turn count is now only used alongside grounding, never alone.

pageDescription: Treat time and financial value as modeled scenarios based on explicit assumptions.
description: Every hours measure reports the same quantity - the full human-equivalent time the delivered work would have taken a person. Per-week measures divide by the weeks in the selected period, not by the weeks a given category happened to appear in, so a breakdown always adds back to the page total.

pageDescription: Treat time and financial value as modeled scenarios based on explicit assumptions.
description: Earlier versions applied a 70% realisation factor to hours and a fixed 50% reinvestment factor to capacity. Both have been removed because neither was traceable to a cited source. Hours and value now report the full estimated human-equivalent effort, and any haircut you want to apply should be an explicit, stated assumption.

pageDescription: Treat time and financial value as modeled scenarios based on explicit assumptions.
description: Full human-equivalent hours multiplied by the hourly value and penalty factor you set. No realisation or reinvestment haircut is applied, so the figure reflects what the delivered work would have cost at the rate supplied.

pageDescription: Treat time and financial value as modeled scenarios based on explicit assumptions.
description: Hours are estimated from a researched band, not a single number. Conservative uses the low end of the band, Typical the midpoint and Optimistic the high end. The Effort scenario slicer on the Estimated Value page switches between them, and every hours and value measure moves with it. Typical is the default. The bands come from the Cowork time-savings methodology, whose primary source is a Microsoft Research difference-in-differences study of 72,186 users.

pageDescription: Treat time and financial value as modeled scenarios based on explicit assumptions.
metric: Why some activities count more than once
description: A single prompt can appear as several rows in the audit log, one per file, page or record it touched. For activities where those rows were verified to be genuinely distinct material - web and enterprise search, file retrieval, document and data analysis, meeting prep, people lookup - effort scales with how much material was handled. For everything else, including general chat, the extra rows are grounding context rather than separate work, so effort is counted once per prompt. Scaling is calibrated to each activity's own average, so the organisation-wide total stays inside the researched band while heavier users are credited more than lighter ones.

pageDescription: Treat time and financial value as modeled scenarios based on explicit assumptions.
description: The parent grouping in the Value Table: 12 tool-agnostic groups - Email, Data & Analysis, Document Creation, Collaboration & Workflows and so on. Each row reaches its Task Category through its Task Breakdown. Cowork is placed by the material the prompt touched - mail items to Email, spreadsheets and data files to Data & Analysis, documents and decks to Document Creation, chat messages to Collaboration & Workflows. Cowork prompts that attach no material stay in General Chat & Q&A, because that is an absence of evidence rather than a category.

Blank means no matched session, not zero reach.

Cowork is priced from its own Cowork task instead. Behavior_Category and Behavior_Enriched are display groupings; they slice the same rows but do not set the baseline.

pageDescription: Trace how observed signals become inferred tasks and modeled value.
metric: App host and the task category
description: Each row is classified first by the resource it touched, such as an email, a meeting, a file or a link. When no resource matches and the enterprise search plugin wasn't used, the open file and then the app host decide the Task Breakdown and its Task Category. For example, Outlook gives Email Drafting or Email Summarising (Email), Excel gives Excel Assistance (Data & Analysis), and Copilot Studio gives Domain-Specific Agent (Specialist Support). If nothing matches, the row is General Chat (General Chat & Q&A).

pageDescription: Trace how observed signals become inferred tasks and modeled value.
description: Because the app host fills in whenever the resource doesn't say, Task Breakdown is inferred largely from the host application rather than the action performed. Creation-heavy work is under-represented relative to summarising and review, so treat the task mix as indicative, not as a measured task census.

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
description: A four-band grade per session - Strong fit, Fair fit, Worth a look, Unclassified - ported from the published Cowork classification methodology's Layer 1 rules. Strong fit: spans two or more apps, builds a file, or uses three or more pieces of material across two or more types (or more than five pieces). Fair fit: some breadth or depth of material and, at Balanced grading, messages read or one app's material. Worth a look: at Balanced grading, chat where nothing was read or attached. Unclassified means the attached material names no application, so it cannot be graded either way - it is an abstention, not a low score. Fit grading in Assumptions sets how strict this is.

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
description: Only typed, non-conversational references count. Chat messages and references the feed left untyped are excluded, because counting them treats talking about work as doing it. In Cowork only 43.5% of the recorded references survive that test. The feed also records a resource type, not an identifier, so five pieces may be five files or one file touched five times - read the grade as work weight, not as a verified count of distinct sources.

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
metric: Why work weight is a floor, not a verdict
description: The published method also grades cross-app work, code, automation and multi-format outputs as Strong fit, and an audit log sees none of them - only 0.23% of threads here touch more than one app, and just 188 rows record a write. The published method's Layer 2 LLM review is absent too. Every one of those gaps can only push a prompt up a band, never down, so the Strong fit share shown is the lowest defensible figure rather than the true one.

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
metric: Counted per prompt, not per audit row
description: A prompt emits one audit row for every reference it attaches, so counting rows lets a heavy prompt vote once per attachment. This page counts distinct prompts instead. The difference is not cosmetic - in Cowork it is 5.4x, and it moved the top-grade share from 75.2% to 21.4% before the material test was applied at all. Pages outside Usage Efficiency and Model Mix still count rows, so task counts there will read higher.

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
metric: Producing a file is not a strong signal
description: In-app Copilots save documents too, so an ordinary file never grades a session Strong fit on its own; it counts only alongside grounding or synthesis evidence. The exception is built or packaged output - an archive, web page, script or structured data file - which no in-app Copilot produces.

pageDescription: Show whether premium model capacity is going to heavy work or to trivia. Tiers come from published list prices; this feed carries no per-call cost.
description: Models grouped into Frontier, Workhorse and Not attributed using published per-million-token list prices. Frontier covers GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5 and Opus 5.5. A model name the rule does not recognise is left Unclassified rather than guessed into a band.

pageDescription: Show whether premium model capacity is going to heavy work or to trivia. Tiers come from published list prices; this feed carries no per-call cost.
description: Share of AI tasks that carry a model name at all. Every frontier figure on this page is stated against that attributed base, never against total tasks, because unattributed rows cannot be assumed to belong to either tier.

pageDescription: Show whether premium model capacity is going to heavy work or to trivia. Tiers come from published list prices; this feed carries no per-call cost.
description: Frontier-tier tasks divided by tasks with a model logged. Read it with attribution coverage beside it; a low share means little when coverage is partial.

pageDescription: Show whether premium model capacity is going to heavy work or to trivia. Tiers come from published list prices; this feed carries no per-call cost.
description: Mean resource references attached per task, compared between tiers. It is the only evidence here that separates heavy work from casual work. It is not a measure of answer quality, it is not a count of verified distinct sources, and it is not a cost.

pageDescription: Show whether premium model capacity is going to heavy work or to trivia. Tiers come from published list prices; this feed carries no per-call cost.
description: The audit feed carries no token counts and no per-call price, so no currency figure is shown against any model or tier. Tier is a relative statement about published list price only.

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
description: The first chart breaks the graded whole into its three bands, so the parts always add back to the total at the left. All graded is every Cowork prompt the rule could grade; Strong fit, Fair fit and Worth a look are mutually exclusive slices of it. Unclassified prompts sit outside the bands and outside the share column, which is why the three bands sum to 100% of graded work rather than to 100% of prompts.

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
description: Counts people, not prompts. A person is habitual if at least 80% of their own graded Cowork prompts graded Worth a look, measured only across people with at least five graded prompts. Volume alone cannot show this - a single enthusiast can produce thousands of light prompts - so each person is banded by their own share instead. Below five graded prompts a share is noise, so those people are excluded from both the numerator and the denominator rather than counted as well-targeted.

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
metric: Why the fit test is scoped to Cowork
description: Light work is only a cost signal on a surface that is paid for separately. On an included Copilot Chat seat a short, ungrounded prompt costs nothing extra and is entirely expected. The same grade therefore means different things on different surfaces, which is why it is applied to Cowork here and to premium models on Model Mix, and why any estate-wide figure is shown as context rather than as a target.

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
metric: Which tool carries the heavier work
description: Read from the grounding ratio - material attached per Cowork prompt divided by material attached per in-app Copilot Chat prompt. Above 1.0 the paid surface is carrying the heavier work; below 1.0 it is carrying the lighter work. The page states whichever direction the data shows rather than assuming the paid surface is the heavier one, because in this tenant it is not.

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
description: A prompt that carried little material - few or no files, links or pasted text - and few turns. It describes the shape of the request, not its worth: a simple ask can still be valuable work. Replaces the older internal term "light work".

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
description: Prompts with enough recorded detail to judge fit. Prompts whose attachments carry no recorded type are left out rather than assumed simple, so every share on this page is a floor, not a verdict. Replaces the older internal term "graded on work weight".

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
description: Each Cowork prompt is mapped to a Cowork task (Cowork Methodology v4) - Analysis & Research, Document & content creation, Email, Communication and so on - read from the material it attached. The source feed tags every Cowork prompt General Chat, a bucket defined as no signals matched, so this is derived here instead.

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
metric: Why Cowork is categorised here and not upstream
description: 49% of Cowork prompts attach a typed resource such as a spreadsheet, deck or PDF, yet all of them arrive tagged General Chat. Left uncorrected the whole surface is valued at the General assistance band, the lowest in the methodology. Three v4 categories - Meetings, Specialized workflows and Code - are not observable in an audit log and are never assigned.

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
description: Cowork sessions carrying enough attached material to grade. Fit is judged per session, not per prompt: a person picks a surface once for a piece of work, and the files are attached at the start, so grading each follow-up turn alone convicted the whole session as light work.

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
description: Grading each prompt alone put 74.5% of assessed work in the lowest grade, 58% of which had attached nothing at all - they were follow-up turns in a session whose material arrived earlier. Same thresholds, moved to session grain.

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
description: Cowork human-equivalent hours priced from the Cowork task its attached material shows, at that task's researched per-turn rate from Human Time Estimates. Replaces the General Chat fallback rate (8 min/turn) the feed forces on every Cowork prompt.

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
description: The cheaper surface for work graded Worth a look, with evidence: how many comparable Copilot Chat prompts the estate already runs on the same task. Blank on Strong and Fair fit, and blank when no comparable Copilot volume exists, so the table never invents an alternative.

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
description: The only two inputs to the fit grade, shown so the grade can be checked rather than trusted. Source items is the average pieces of material a session worked across - files, links and pasted text, not just file attachments - so it measures depth. Source types is how many different types those were, so it measures breadth. Fit rises with both: Strong fit needs 3+ items across 2+ types, or more than 5 items on depth alone (or work that spans apps or builds a file). Worth a look carries none - and, at Balanced grading, no messages read either. Expert Equivalent Hours was removed from these tables: it is an outcome of the work, not evidence of how it graded.

pageDescription: Show whether premium model capacity is going to heavy work or to trivia. Tiers come from published list prices; this feed carries no per-call cost.
description: Premium-tier work in this estate is 100% Cowork and mid-cost work is 100% other tools, so cost tier and tool are the same split. A premium-versus-mid comparison would mostly compare Cowork with Copilot, not one model with another. Model fit is therefore judged inside Cowork only, where the model choice is actually made.

pageDescription: Show whether premium model capacity is going to heavy work or to trivia. Tiers come from published list prices; this feed carries no per-call cost.
description: Sessions on a Frontier (premium cost) model whose work graded Worth a look. A prompt to test a lighter model, not proof one would have answered as well. Formerly Try cheaper (over-specified).

pageDescription: Show whether premium model capacity is going to heavy work or to trivia. Tiers come from published list prices; this feed carries no per-call cost.
description: Judged sessions whose model cost tier suits the fit grade of the work: a Frontier (premium cost) model on Strong or Fair fit work, or a mid-cost model on Fair fit or Worth a look work. Premium capacity going where the evidence supports it.

pageDescription: Show whether premium model capacity is going to heavy work or to trivia. Tiers come from published list prices; this feed carries no per-call cost.
description: The mid-cost model this estate already runs for the same kind of Cowork task, with the volume that proves it. Mid-cost models carry only 254 Cowork prompts in total, so read this as 'a cheaper model has handled this work', not as a benchmark. Blank on well-matched rows and blank where no mid-cost volume exists.

pageDescription: Show whether premium model capacity is going to heavy work or to trivia. Tiers come from published list prices; this feed carries no per-call cost.
description: Both compared premium against mid-cost tiers, which in this estate is a Cowork-versus-Copilot comparison wearing a model label. The two visuals were removed rather than left to read as a model finding. The measures remain in the model, unused by any page.

pageDescription: Explore established usage patterns. Stage boundaries remain the inherited, unconfirmed mapping.
description: Inactive reads N/A when the cohort is Cowork. Inactive means holds a seat but did not use it, and only Copilot has a seat inventory in this model - the Cowork cohort filters the audit feed, not the licence list, so the figure would subtract 183 Cowork-active users from 11,442 Copilot seats and report 11,316 against an observed Cowork population of 186. With Inactive blank the stage base falls back to users active last month, so Beginner and Developing are shares of the people actually observed on Cowork.

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
description: The test inside the fit grade that decided most sessions in the row, with the share it covers. Reads the rule that fired - spans apps, built an artifact, multi-source synthesis, mixed sources, messages read, one app or chat only. It is counted from the graded sessions, not inferred, and it is why the same task can be Strong fit in one row and Worth a look in another - the difference is always the material the session worked across.

pageDescription: Separate two efficiency questions - was the work billed to the right tool, and was the model heavier than the task needed.
description: How strict the Cowork Fit and Model Fit grade is, set by the Fit Grading column in Assumptions. Balanced (default): messages read and one-app work count as Fair fit, so Worth a look is kept for chat where nothing was read or attached. Lenient: a longer chat with nothing attached is Fair too. Strict: the original rule - chat only or one app is Worth a look. The grade sees which apps, files and messages a session touched, not prompt text or answer quality, so a flag is a coaching prompt, not a verdict on Cowork's value.
